name: Greenish Slate-Black
lede: Greenish Slate-Black is a very dark, greened grey named for the rock, slate, standing almost on top of Dark Slate Grey and Bluish Slate-Black in the ISCC-NBS system's 1955 list.

sections.title: A near-black slate
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* records this hue at plate XLVIII, hue 37″″, tone m [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 filed it in block 151, a dark grayish green, alongside several near-identical dark slates [2]. Slate, the fine-grained rock split into thin dark sheets for roofing, is dark grey with a slight cast of color depending on the quarry; this name leans that cast toward green [2].

The nearest named colors are [[dark-slate-grey|Dark Slate Grey]], 3.0 units away, and [[bluish-slate-black|Bluish Slate-Black]], 3.1 units away and bluer; at this lightness, 29 on a 0–100 scale, small shifts in hue produce several different names for what the eye reads as one near-black [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Greenish Slate-Black appears in 421 of our 23,781 paintings, as photographed, more common than 70 percent of the archive's named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 45 of 1,674 paintings, at 3.0 times the expected rate, and Paul Cézanne is its most devoted painter, carrying it in 8 of his 50 works here, 7.4 times his museums' baseline [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, buried in shadow [3]. The earliest match is dated 1099, 813 years before Ridgway's 1912 record — a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof that slate pigment reached that canvas, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].
